title: John Carroll (1789)
hookLine: the priests of a new country choose their own bishop, a friend of religious liberty

lines: THEY VOTE FOR ONE OF THEIR OWN.
cards: A letter goes from a small group of priests in the new United States to Rome, with an unusual question. The country has just won its independence.
Its Catholics are few, often distrusted, scattered across farms and port towns, with no bishop of their own. Rome could simply appoint one and send him over. Instead, the priests ask: may we choose?
The answer comes back yes. They vote, and pick a Maryland man who had once been a Jesuit, a cousin of a signer of the Declaration of Independence. His name is John Carroll.

teach.b: First, the loss. He trained as a Jesuit in Europe and was teaching there when the pope suppressed the Society of Jesus. The life he had chosen was dissolved.
He came home to Maryland as a parish priest with no community, riding out to say Mass in family houses. Second, the revolution. When the colonies broke with Britain, he sided with independence.

Congress even sent him with Benjamin Franklin on a mission to Canada, hoping a Catholic priest might win over Catholic Canadians. It didn't work, but it put him at the center of the new nation's life. Third, the bishop.
Chosen by his fellow priests and confirmed by the pope, he became bishop of Baltimore, a diocese that stretched across the whole country.
He gave much of his energy to schools, and founded the academy that became Georgetown.
Fourth, the freedom. Carroll argued that the new republic should protect every citizen's conscience, and that Catholics should be free to worship and serve their country like anyone else.
He saw religious liberty as something Catholics could hold to, not just tolerate.

teach.h: WHERE THE SPIRIT OF THE LORD IS, THERE IS LIBERTY.
teach.b: Saint Paul writes in his second letter to the Corinthians, in the Douay-Rheims: "where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty." Carroll's hope was a land where faith did not need a king's permission.

how: Catholics in the United States remember John Carroll at Baltimore's basilica and at Georgetown, and parishes in the United States pray for the nation at Mass on Independence Day and Thanksgiving.

games.q: you're one of a few Catholic priests in the newly independent United States, with no bishop. Rome is asking how one should be chosen. what do you propose?
o: let Rome pick someone from Europe and send him.
let the priests here elect one of their own.
do without a bishop for now.
games.why: they asked to choose, Rome said yes, and they voted for John Carroll. the pope then confirmed him as bishop of Baltimore.

practice: Think of one freedom you used today without noticing: speaking your mind, walking into a church, a mosque, a temple, or none at all, reading what you chose. Then think of someone, near or far, who doesn't have that freedom.
If you pray, pray for your country and for them; if you don't, hold both in mind, side by side.

wordCard.voice: John Carroll. The Maryland priest whose fellow priests chose him as their bishop, a founder of schools and a friend of religious liberty.

orig.note: Latin: liberty, freedom, the word in the Latin Bible's line where the Spirit of the Lord is.

carryVoice: Your line: a new land. His fellow priests chose him, and Rome said yes. That's day eight hundred seventy-nine.
